{

  "scope": {
    "machine": "FISHER_CC9",

  },
  "failure_pattern": {
    "cluster_key": "75c7bfffb16639e2",
    "failure_stage": "PHYSICAL_RESOLUTION",
    "failure_reason": "OWNER_CONFLICT",
    "catalog_signature": "1794-IB16",
    "direction_evidence_class": "I",
    "bank_relationship_class": "UNBOUND"
  },
  "affected_count": 2,
  "observed_facts": [
    "Both affected raw claims use the identical address tuple: FISHER_CC9, word 1070, bit 3.",
    "The source rows are distinct: Conveyor.asc rows 888 and 1412, with distinct IO names and descriptions.",
    "Configio word 1070 has Low bank 144 with description 1794-IB16-211. The independently derived rack evidence identifies an input 1794-IB16 module with input bank 144.",
    "The High half of word 1070 is bank 145 and has no hardware-bank match.",
    "One-sided binding is established elsewhere: traces for words 100 and 101 accept their Low-bank matches and reject their unmatched High halves. An unmatched High half must not be used to select another module or an owner."
  ],
  "evidence_refs": [
    "get_source_rows(FORTNA/Conveyor.asc, 888)",
    "get_source_rows(FORTNA/Conveyor.asc, 1412)",
    "get_configio_word(1070)",
    "get_configio_binding_trace(1070)",
    "get_adapter_modules(T_1794_AENT_7)",
    "get_eip_bank_map()",
    "get_configio_binding_trace(100)",
    "get_configio_binding_trace(101)"
  ],
  "candidate_rule_name": "duplicate_word_bit_owner_conflict_requires_review",
  "candidate_rule_description": "When two or more raw physical claims share the same machine, Configio word, and bit, and independent directional bank/catalog evidence establishes one hardware context, preserve that context for investigation but do not select an owning claim. Mark every claim in the collision group REVIEW_REQUIRED.",
  "proposed_inputs": {
    "claim_fields": [
      "machine",
      "word",
      "bit",
      "claim_id"
    ],
    "configio_fields": [
      "Octal_Word",
      "Bank",
      "LoHi",
      "Desc",
      "Interface"
    ],
    "hardware_fields": [
      "catalog",
      "direction",
      "input_bank",
      "output_bank",
      "data_index",
      "physical_slot"
    ],
    "preconditions": [
      "At least two distinct claim IDs share an identical machine, word, and bit.",
      "An exact directional bank match and catalog-compatible module context is independently established.",
      "No authoritative source specifies ownership precedence for the colliding claims."
    ]
  },
  "proposed_transformation": [
    "Group raw physical claims by machine, word, and bit before selecting an owner.",
    "Use only exact directional bank and catalog-compatible evidence to establish the shared hardware context.",
    "When group cardinality exceeds one, retain every claim and set each disposition to REVIEW_REQUIRED.",
    "Do not select an owner using IO name, description, source-row order, or an unmatched opposite LoHi half.",
    "Do not cross-bind an unmatched High half to a Low-side module."
  ],
  "expected_outputs": {
    "disposition": "REVIEW_REQUIRED",
    "owner_selection": "none",
    "hardware_assignment_effect": "no new hardware assignment"
  },
  "supporting_examples": [
    {
      "claims": [
        "cl_400800a0312e67f0",
        "cl_8016c90b60a1f13a"
      ],
      "address_tuple": {
        "machine": "FISHER_CC9",
        "word": 1070,
        "bit": 3
      },
      "raw_source_rows": [
        888,
        1412
      ],
      "evidence": "Both claims collide on the same raw tuple. Word 1070 Low bank 144 has an exact compatible input-bank match for 1794-IB16; the source supplies no ownership-precedence fact."
    }
  ],
  "counterexamples": [
    {
      "word": 100,
      "observation": "Low bank 130 is accepted while High bank 131 has no bank match. The accepted module is output-directional, demonstrating that unmatched High halves are not inferred as a second binding."
    },
    {
      "word": 101,
      "observation": "Low bank 132 is accepted while High bank 133 has no bank match, independently repeating the one-sided binding shape."
    },
    {
      "word": 1070,
      "observation": "High bank 145 has no bank match; it cannot establish an alternative module context or resolve ownership between the two colliding claims."
    }
  ],
  "ambiguities": [
    "This cluster contains only one duplicate address tuple, so it supports a narrow collision-preservation rule, not a general semantic ownership-precedence rule.",
    "Neither raw claim name nor description is authoritative evidence that one claim should supersede the other."
  ],
  "additional_evidence_needed": [
    "Verified Fortna design documentation or another authoritative source defining ownership precedence for duplicate machine/word/bit claims, if a single owner must be selected."
  ],
  "tests_required": [
    "Group all physical claims by machine, word, and bit before any ownership decision.",
    "Verify both word-1070 bit-3 claims remain REVIEW_REQUIRED and that no winner is emitted.",
    "Regression-test words 100 and 101 to ensure unmatched High halves are not cross-bound.",
    "Reject implementations that select an owner using source ordering, IO name, or description."
  ],
  "confidence": {
    "level": "HIGH",
    "basis": "The address collision is direct raw-source evidence. The Low-bank hardware context is independently corroborated by Configio, rack-module, and aggregate bank-map evidence. No evidence establishes an ownership-precedence convention."
  }
}
